fn:servo_test/diag.py::cmd.explain: Sends MAV_CMD_DO_SET_SERVO for output ch with pulse width pwm in microseconds (no acknowledgement awaited).

mod:servo_test/diag14.py.explain: Checks that output 14 (AUX6) really sends the commanded pulse: asks for SERVO_OUTPUT_RAW at 20 Hz, then commands 1900, 1400, 1750 and 1100 us on outputs 9 and 14 and prints the newest readback of each after 1.2 s.

mod:servo_test/servo_control.py.explain: Command-line tool to drive any output with DO_SET_SERVO (default output 2 = MAIN OUT 2): --pwm sends one value, --sweep opens (1900 us) and closes (1400 us) 3 times, --interactive lets you type pulse widths, and --setup sets SERVO2_FUNCTION to 0 and reboots the flight controller. Every command waits up to 3 s for the autopilot's COMMAND_ACK and prints it.

fn:servo_test/servo_control.py::connect.explain: Opens the MAVLink link with pymavlink, waits up to 15 s for a heartbeat (exits if none), and uses system 1 / component 1 if the heartbeat came from system 0.

fn:servo_test/servo_control.py::set_serv.explain: Sends MAV_CMD_DO_SET_SERVO (output number, pulse width in microseconds) and waits up to 3 s for COMMAND_ACK; prints the result name and returns True only if it was ACCEPTED.
Calls set_servo for every output in the list.

fn:servo_test/servo_control.py::sweep.explain: For each cycle and each group of outputs: open (high pulse width), wait `dwell` seconds, close (low pulse width), wait again.

fn:servo_test/servo_control.py::interact.explain: Asks for pulse widths in a loop (prompt 'ch[2] pwm> ') and sends each one to the chosen outputs; 'q', 'quit', 'exit' or Ctrl-D stops it.

fn:servo_test/servo_control.py::set_para.explain: Sets a flight-controller parameter (a 32-bit float unless another type is given) and prints the PARAM_VALUE answer.

fn:servo_test/servo_control.py::setup.explain: For each output in MANAGED (only output 2): frees its pin from the button feature if a BTN parameter is listed (none is), sets SERVO2_FUNCTION = 0 so DO_SET_SERVO can drive it, then reboots the flight controller.
fn:servo_test/servo_control.py::setup.effects: Changes a flight-controller parameter and reboots it.

fn:servo_test/servo_control.py::main.explain: Reads the options (--device, --baud, --channels or --channel, --pwm, --sweep with --low 1400 --high 1900 --cycles 3 --dwell 1.0, --interactive, --setup), connects, and runs the chosen action; prints a hint when no action was given.

mod:servo_wiggle.py.explain: A tiny pymavlink bench script at the repo root (no ROS, no options): it connects to the Pixhawk on /dev/ttyUSB0 at 115200 baud, waits for a heartbeat, then swings servo OUTPUT 13 between 1417 and 1583 microseconds (1500 plus or minus 15 degrees at about 5.6 us per degree) once a second, until Ctrl+C sends it back to 1500 us. Its settings are constants at the top of the file.
mod:servo_wiggle.py.how_it_fits: A TOOL like the scripts in servo_test/, not part of the flight or the simulator. Output 13 is the tent payload's release servo in flight (main_controller opens it at 1400 us), so do not run it with a payload loaded; MAVROS (launcher.sh) must be stopped first, because only one program can own the serial port. The stray copy servo_wiggle.py' (with an apostrophe in its name) is an older version.

fn:servo_wiggle.py::set_servo.explain: Sends one COMMAND_LONG MAV_CMD_DO_SET_SERVO to system 1, component 1: output SERVO_CHANNEL (13) to the given pulse width in microseconds. It does not wait for an acknowledgement.
fn:servo_wiggle.py::set_servo.called_when: once a second in the script's endless loop (1417, then 1583), and once with 1500 when Ctrl+C stops it
fn:servo_wiggle.py::set_servo.effects: MAVLink command to the flight controller: the servo on output 13 moves

mod:servo_wiggle.py'.explain: A stray older copy of servo_wiggle.py (the apostrophe is part of the file name, probably a typing slip). It drives output 10 instead of 13 and swings between 1500 and 1833 microseconds (60 degrees, starting at the centre); nothing runs or imports it.

pkg:scripts.explain: Small operator tools at the repo root: humanize.sh (readable clock times in launcher.sh's output), watch_status.sh + watch_status.py (show every ground-station message and camera status line in a terminal, for example over SSH on the Jetson) and check_versions.sh (list software versions to compare the dev container with the Jetson).
pkg:scripts.how_it_fits: launcher.sh sends all of its output through humanize.sh unless ASTRA_RAW_TIME is set. watch_status listens to /mavros/statustext/send (what the team nodes send to Mission Planner), /mavros/statustext/recv (what ArduPilot sends) and video_cam's /camera/status. None of these tools change the drone; they only read and print.

mod:scripts/check_versions.sh.explain: Prints one line per piece of software with its installed version: machine type, OS, JetPack (L4T), ROS distro, MAVROS, cv_bridge, mavlink-router, RMW, gcc, cmake, OpenCV, TensorRT, onnxruntime, CUDA, Python, numpy, torch (with cuda or cpu), torchvision, ultralytics, sahi, pymavlink, MAVProxy and watchdog. Run it in the dev container and on the Jetson and compare (diff) the two outputs.
mod:scripts/check_versions.sh.how_it_fits: Helps keep the dev container (docker/Dockerfile) matching the Jetson (pins in requirements_jetson.txt); the root README.md mentions it, and the version notes at the top of docker/Dockerfile were read off the Jetson with it on 2026-10-10.

fn:scripts/check_versions.sh::row.explain: Prints one table row: the name padded to 22 characters, then the value, or 'not installed' when the value is empty.

fn:scripts/check_versions.sh::pyver.explain: Prints the __version__ of a Python module (for example numpy) using python3, or nothing if the module cannot be imported.

fn:scripts/check_versions.sh::debver.explain: Prints the version of an installed Ubuntu/Debian package (with dpkg-query), or nothing if it is not installed.

mod:scripts/humanize.sh.explain: A text filter (awk): it reads lines from its input and replaces every 10-digit epoch time with a fraction, such as the ROS log stamp [1782434179.406602296], with the local clock time [17:36:19] (using the computer's time-zone offset), printing each line straight away.
mod:scripts/humanize.sh.how_it_fits: launcher.sh runs 'exec > >(scripts/humanize.sh) 2>&1', so everything it and its nodes print passes through this filter; set ASTRA_RAW_TIME=1 to see the raw times.

mod:scripts/watch_status.py.explain: A listen-only ROS node ('status_tap') that prints every STATUSTEXT the team nodes send (TX, /mavros/statustext/send), every STATUSTEXT ArduPilot sends (RX, /mavros/statustext/recv) and every /camera/status line (CAM), each with the time and severity, in colour when printing to a terminal. Options: --send-only, --topic NAME (more std_msgs/String topics), --no-color.
mod:scripts/watch_status.py.how_it_fits: An operator's window into the mission (for example 'Camera trigger STARTED', 'SUCCESS: Captured 2K image #12', 'CMD SUCCESS: autofocus'); started by watch_status.sh.

fn:scripts/watch_status.py::StatusTap.explain: The listen-only node 'status_tap': its subscriptions and a printing helper.

fn:scripts/watch_status.py::StatusTap.__.explain: Creates the subscriptions: /mavros/statustext/send always; /mavros/statustext/recv (best-effort, to match MAVROS) and /camera/status unless --send-only; one more std_msgs/String subscription per --topic. It turns colour on only for a real terminal and prints 'status tap running - Ctrl-C to stop'.

fn:scripts/watch_status.py::StatusTap.on.explain: Turns a StatusText into a printed line: the tag (TX or RX), the severity name (0 EMERG ... 4 WARN, 5 NOTICE, 6 INFO, 7 DEBUG) and the text.

fn:scripts/watch_status.py::StatusTap.em.explain: Prints one line 'HH:MM:SS TAG note text', with dim and colour codes (TX cyan, RX magenta, CAM green) when colour is on, and flushes it at once.

fn:scripts/watch_status.py::main.explain: Reads the options --send-only, --topic and --no-color, starts ROS 2, spins the StatusTap node until Ctrl-C, then shuts down cleanly.

mod:scripts/watch_status.sh.explain: Loads ROS 2 Humble (/opt/ros/humble/setup.bash; stops with an error if it is missing) and, if the workspace has been built, ros2_ws/install/setup.bash, then starts watch_status.py with the same options.
mod:scripts/watch_status.sh.how_it_fits: The one command a person runs, locally or with ssh on the Jetson, to watch the mission's messages: './scripts/watch_status.sh'.
